unspecified.behavior: The drawing margin (half the scroller's visible height) is computed once, when the IntersectionObserver is created (dependencies `[firstRatio, state.numPages]`, PdfPagesPanel.tsx:134-157). It is not recomputed when the window is resized or the phone sheet changes height.

scores.reason: After a resize or a change in sheet height, thumbnails start drawing earlier or later than the half-height rule says, so white faces show briefly while scrolling.

Confirmed at PdfPagesPanel.tsx:139-151: the rootMargin is computed once when the observer is created (deps [firstRatio, state.numPages]), so after the window is resized or the phone sheet changes height, pages start drawing a little earlier or later than half a visible height away; at worst the user sees a brief white placeholder before a thumbnail appears, because cells still draw once they intersect the visible box.

unspecified.behavior: Cells in `drawing` do not count toward the 120-page cap (PdfPagesPanel.tsx:200 reads only `drawn.size`). A fast scroll can therefore mount more than 120 `<Page>` renders before eviction trims `drawn`; the layout-effect change only removes the one-frame overshoot of `drawn` itself.

scores.reason: Flinging through a long PDF briefly holds more rasters in memory than the cap. Nothing visible changes.

Confirmed at PdfPagesPanel.tsx:200 and 313-321: eviction checks only drawn.size, and cells in `entered` mount a <Page> without counting against the cap, so a fast fling through a long PDF's rail starts renders for every page passed; pdf.js then does wasted work and the rail may lag briefly before eviction brings drawn back to 120, but nothing visible is wrong and I3's cap on `drawn` still holds.
